reason: The trigger is a native <button type="button"> carrying aria-expanded and an aria-controls naming the region it shows and hides; the region is always rendered, so aria-controls never points at nothing, and it is hidden by `hidden` and by the inline display together because an inline display:flex beats [hidden]'s UA display:none. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED IS TREEVIEW. With arbitrary nesting the rendered structure resembles one, and APG's treeview would demand aria-level on every node, a roving tab stop and four-direction arrow navigation. None of that is designed here and none of it is bound: each collapsible is an independent disclosure, which is what a nav landmark full of links actually is. The cost of that choice is the cost the disclosure pattern's own description states -- no aria-level, no arrow keys, no set-size information -- and a reader of this binding alone should take it as refused rather than missing. The two keyboard requirements are met by the platform rather than by Arena: a native button routes Enter and Space to a click, and nothing here intercepts either key. frameworks/react/components/navigation/arena-side-nav/ArenaSideNav.disclosure.dom.test.tsx is the proof standing above every claim in this file.
